wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.ephemeral_event: Transient sync/federation/app signal; MUST NOT be persisted as durable Event Envelope history.

admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.did_root_anchor: Admitted only by the closed identity-root anchor verifier. v1 permits this class for a self-principal PCR genesis ak.realm.create bound to entry 0 through one critical did_inception ref, and for B-model ak.device.reanchor bound to the accepted registry head through one critical did_recovery_anchor ref. This verifier is the sole exception to generic Event verification_method-controller equality: verification_method MUST instead equal an active controller-proof verification method from the referenced entry, and the verifier validates it against the accepted did:webvh history/update authority without rewriting its did:key controller to actor_id. Root/update authority MUST NOT authorize any other Event kind. Batch shape, DID history, active update authority, full frontier CAS and conflict-slot checks remain mandatory.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a principal_control ak.realm.create with no did_inception ref and with both executed_by and authorization_ref. The verifier MUST prove actor_id is a managed Agent or explicitly organization-governed principal, resolve authorization_ref in that actor DID's accepted ArkretPrincipalControlRealm/controller delegation, require realm_id and payload.object.id to equal the delegated PCR binding, require proof.verification_method to resolve to executed_by or its current authorized device, and reject self-principal or generic realm.create-capability substitution. This class never authorizes the following device authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by one or more named capability actions listed in admission_capabilities. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant per capability-action-registry. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Standard ak.* effect kinds MUST appear in this registry when used by a DataEvent effect, Control Move effect, or Event Envelope payload router.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.
Entries with wire_scope=ephemeral_event MUST be carried only on ephemeral channels and MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root, or reducer state.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

Every active lifecycle event kind MUST declare lifecycle_modality. Use reversible for a reversible lifecycle facet or either member of an archive/restore pair, and terminal for an irreversible transition that cannot be restored. Reducers and SDKs MUST NOT infer modality from event-kind spelling or the presence of a sibling event.

Every active reducer-input durable kind MUST declare plane, sealed, and a complete machine-readable cell contract. A single-target kind MAY use the legacy cell_family/cell_subject/lattice/bottom shorthand. cell_writes[] is the general authority and is REQUIRED for multi-target kinds; each entry declares cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, optional initial_value, and optional condition. A condition marks the target as conditional: it uses the closed grammar {kind: field_present|field_absent|field_equals|any_field_present, field: <dot-path>, const?: <scalar>, fields?: [<dot-path>...]} evaluated as a pure function of the schema-validated payload. When the condition holds the target is required and the Event MUST carry exactly one matching effect; when it does not hold the Event MUST NOT carry that effect. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2. The generator materializes the single-target shorthand when cell_writes[] has one entry. cell_family is a stable ak.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, an explicitly sourced payload.* or envelope.actor_id field path, a coalesce descriptor, or a composite descriptor. Bare field paths and other envelope.* fields are invalid. plane MUST be data or control; sealed is a boolean and MUST be true iff plane=control. plane/sealed are the machine-readable authority for DataEvent versus Control Move routing and plane_cross_write validation; payload prose is explanatory. bottom is reject, expose, or inert; inert MUST be used when the lattice cannot produce Bottom. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any effect has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` implements singleton-once-set cells.

Protocol-singleton cells MAY take their genesis value from a create payload, but every subsequent write MUST use a registered event_kind. ak.component.notary.v1 is canonically defined in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 6.5; its genesis value comes from ak.realm.create and subsequent writes use ak.realm.notary.

Lattice MUST be one of the fully specified core types: or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log. A new lattice type cannot become active until its join, bottom, op schema, profile gate, and conformance vectors are all registered.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent effects are locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move effects are finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST list the authorizing action(s) in admission_capabilities. Enforced by lint_artifacts.py; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

A conditional admission MUST use only selectors defined by admission_predicate_contract. All non-otherwise predicates are evaluated independently; exactly one match selects its branch, zero matches selects the final otherwise branch, and multiple matches fail closed. otherwise is never evaluated as an ordinary predicate.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.

event_kinds.payload: Organization-authorized Realm relationship statement or revocation

Typed Realm link graph edge. link_kind declares governance / discoverability / import-export / confidential-extension semantics; it is never generic parent/child containment and never implicitly propagates membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Realm preview / peek policy for directory card, stripped state, history stub, and plaintext history snippet projections

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer. payload = {realm_id, strand_id}; reducer projects payload.strand_id into the Realm projection default_strand_id (single authoritative pointer; avoids multi-default dirty state). Reducer MUST verify the referenced strand_id already exists in this Realm (a projected, non-tombstoned Strand); a dangling reference MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. Strand-side is_default is a derived marker (strand_id == realm.default_strand_id), never independent storage; clients discover the default Strand deterministically from the Realm projection default_strand_id or the Strand projection is_default, NOT from any UUID-reuse implementation detail. Authorization is the standard Realm-admin gate (hold ak.realm.admin, or the same-name action ak.realm.set_default_strand).
CAS rotation of the per-Realm notary authority. The current notary must finalize the Move; concurrent rotations join to Bottom and require recovery.
Profile-gated transition from the Realm's current digest suite to a stronger active suite, bound to a transition snapshot and dual-root Seal under ak.profile.hash_transition.v1.
Enabled Realm policy components set. Payload MUST carry monotonic policy_revision; reducer rejects rollback or gaps and policy_frontier_digest MUST cover policy_revision.

Constraints on member delivery_binding: which binding_source values are admissible, which recipient services are allowed, which endorsers are required, whether DID Document fallback / unroutable membership are permitted, who may sign rebind. Governs reducer acceptance of ak.member.state{membership=join}.delivery_binding (see governance/join-policy.md §5.1).
Realm read receipt disclosure policy (disclosure / visibility / scope_overrides_allowed / receipt_compliance_opt_in); see zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5 for the closed compliance opt-in object
Realm moderation policy (blocklists, allowlists, content filters)
Plaintext-visible services declaration outside E2EE boundary
Per-parent inheritance policy; one entry per source Realm
Realm tombstone lifecycle facet (terminal pointer to successor)
Realm destroy lifecycle facet (terminal decommission marker)
Circle create (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary). Initializes independent MLS group and epoch-0 governance binding only when encryption_profile=mls_rfc9420. See zh/models/circle.md §3, §5.

Full ak.schema.agent_sidecar.v1 object. Accepted only inside the atomic ak.self.agent.sidecar.command.ensure aggregate after its reducer-derived backing Circle exists. The canonical Event materializes backing_circle_id and is stamped into that Circle effective scope; raw ensure callers cannot supply it. See zh/models/sidecar.md §2-§5.
Circle patch (ak.patch.v1 with path NOT containing realm_id / encryption_profile). Modifies title / summary / display / directory_visibility / join_rule / history_visibility.
Circle tombstone (terminal). Triggers lifecycle cascade per zh/models/circle.md §9.2.

Circle membership state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ak.member.state (invite/join/knock/leave/ban), scoped to a Circle. Reducer MUST first validate the target actor is a parent Realm `join` member, otherwise failed_precondition reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

Reducer-derived: Circle sub-seal commits opaque sub_seal_head_digest to the Realm Seal stream at the Circle's profile-defined cadence. MUST use time-based ticks + empty-batch commitment to avoid leaking activity frequency. See zh/models/circle.md §10.2.

Issuer-signed endorsement that a subject DID (typically an agent / service / hosted actor) is accountable_principal_ids the issuer for a declared scope (employment / contracted_service / agent_operator / etc.). Required to verify `Actor Profile.accountable_principal_ids[]` entries; reducer strips unverified DIDs from accountable_principal_ids. See zh/models/actor.md §3.3.1. expires_at is optional; absent means non-expiring, governed by grant_status revocation and controller lifecycle cascade.

Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.

Realm-scoped MemberIdentity segment replacement event. Append-only log entry that may supersede prior ak.member.identity.update events via payload.replaces[] without overloading ak.profile.update patch semantics.

Strand business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at; ak.strand.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on the Strand's discussion track that 'references' this event, and the event log's own actor_id / created_at is the audit source. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=strand_already_terminal; state=archived yields strand_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond these hard invariants.

Unified Strand tracks patch. payload.patch uses ak.patch.v1 against the Strand.tracks map: keys are track names (e.g. `synthesis`, `discussion`), values are patch ops that may toggle enabled, set is_primary, or modify profile / metadata on a track entry. Atomic across multiple tracks.

Strand move between Spaces (target_space_id in payload). Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (board_space_id, strand_id); the contains Relation list_space_id->strand_id is derived from cell value, not a separate truth source. Plane ruling (CBA): ak.component.strand.position.v1 defaults to sealed=true (control plane), so ak.strand.move is a Control Move carrying seal_basis; Realm schema MAY redeclare the cell family as data-plane mv_register + user-pick or per-object sequencer per authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.4 and models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6.

Strand reorder within Space. Writes the same cell as ak.strand.move; effect.list_space_id MUST equal head_eq.list_space_id (rank-only update). Plane ruling follows ak.strand.move: same cell family, same default sealed=true control-plane declaration (models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6).

Set or clear a per-(strand, actor) watch subscription. Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (strand_id, watcher_actor_id). Payload carries level in {mentions_only, participating, all, muted} (or null to clear, equivalent to mentions_only). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds ak.strand.watch.set.others. Cross-actor writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ak.audit.accessed event with access_kind=watch_set_others. The watches Relation (actor --watches--> strand) is a derived projection of this cell, not a separate truth source — direct ak.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.
Space create (board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket / etc.)
Space metadata update (title, rank, kind-specific fields)

Space parent declaration. Parent is another ak:space: or null; cross-Realm parent is navigation only and never propagates Realm membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Space archive (UI-level grouping archive; contained Strands MUST be relocated or follow archive)
Space restore (transition state archived -> active; only valid when current state == archived; tombstoned Spaces MUST NOT be restored)
Space tombstone (irreversible; contained Strands MUST be relocated before)

Controller-authored durable Sidecar exchange control. The outer payload exposes only private Strand routing plus an MLS encrypted payload whose plaintext validates as ak.schema.agent_sidecar_exchange_control.v1. It is accepted only in the matching Sidecar backing Circle from that Sidecar controller and is the sole truth source for coordinator reassignment and terminal exchange state.
Message-scoped redaction; does not grant generic redaction authority
Generic redaction envelope for non-message objects/events and profile-declared content trimming

Morph schema_refs[] migration. First-class event for evolving a Morph's schema_refs[] without bypassing audit / capability gates. Carries (from_schema_refs[], to_schema_refs[], compatibility_class, migration_evidence?). Required capability ak.morph.schema_migrate (high risk tier; see capability-action-registry.json). compatibility_class = additive | breaking | transformation; core reducers MUST reject breaking/transformation unless the Realm declares ak.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3.

Morph business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at; ak.morph.update / ak.morph.schema_migrate patches on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on an associated discussion track that 'references' this event. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=morph_already_terminal; state=archived yields morph_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, and approval_evidence; expires_at is optional (absent means non-expiring, revocation-governed). The agent-key cell is an observed-remove OR-Set. First authorization adds one authorization dot. Same-key re-authorization MUST atomically remove every active authorization dot visible at the Move seal_basis and add the replacement dot; it MUST NOT select a winner by arrival time. Concurrent replacement dots that survive the join are evaluated by the deterministic strictest fold: intersect agent_key_scope and audience, take the earliest finite expires_at (absence is +infinity), and fail closed if accountable_principal_id or verification_method disagree. Key replacement has no dedicated rotate kind: runtime replacement re-pairing authorizes the new key and revokes every prior active key (reason=superseded_by_repairing) in the same accepted transaction.

Agent signing key revocation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_revoke_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, revoked_at, and revoked_by; the revocation's control-plane basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and its cutoff is the accepted Seal covering the Move.

Controller-owned signed selector statement binding (controller_subject, agent_slug) to one native personal agent DID. The Event belongs in the controller Principal Control Realm, never the Agent PCR or a Collaboration Realm. Concurrent distinct current values remain visible and make selector resolution ambiguous/fail-closed.

Agent lifecycle transition to paused state. Authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; payload carries no independent frontier. Auth Server MUST reject new agent session grants for this principal; existing tokens fail closed within an independent pause revocation freshness window of at most 60 seconds, never merely the session maximum TTL. Reversible via ak.self.agent.resume.

Agent lifecycle transition from paused to active. Authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; payload carries no independent frontier. At acceptance the reducer MUST use the accepted current control frontier to re-validate controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability_grant freshness; any failure rejects the resume.

Agent lifecycle terminal state. MUST fan-out ak.agent.key.revoke for all active agent keys, ak.capability.revoke for all unrevoked grants, and runtime endpoint revocation. Terminal — no transition out.

Agent-initiated draft proposal. Submitted by agent runtime; Principal Server materializes accepted drafts into controller-owned ak.agent.draft.v1 account-data after capability / policy / accountability / risk check. MUST NOT enter shared Realm history.
Agent-initiated action request. Carries proposed_action, target descriptor, and content digest. Awaits controller approval before generating shared event.

Controller approval of a draft / action request. Binds draft_id, content digest, target descriptor, proposed_action, approved payload digest, approval expiry, and single-use nonce. Publish executor MUST atomic-consume the nonce; reuse fails closed (reason=approval_already_consumed).
Controller rejection of a draft / action request. Draft transitions to rejected; agent runtime MUST NOT continue publish attempts.
Holder-private consent declaration: 'I consent to receive <consent_scope> from <peer>'
Revoke a previously granted consent (shares the ak.consent.grant cell; semantically a remove on the consent or_set)
Principal-scoped contact request fact. Issuer is requester; target holder must respond with accepted/rejected.
Principal-scoped contact acceptance fact. Issuer is original request target and MUST reference target-controlled consent grants.
Principal-scoped contact rejection fact. Issuer is original request target and does not write consent.
Principal-scoped contact tombstone fact. Issuer ends their own side of a contact and may revoke contact-managed consent dots.
Principal-scoped binding from unordered participant pair to canonical DM Realm and main Strand.
Realm-scoped profile override. payload.target_realm_id is the target Realm and no Space boundary is created.

B-model DID-root recovery re-anchor. Accepted only as the first event of an atomic re-anchor plus replacement-authorize unit in a principal control Realm. It fences the old device generation against the complete accepted Seal frontier and preserves every same-version candidate for deterministic conflict quarantine.
Key backup active series selection for one principal and backup_kind.

Push route binding for a (recipient_service_id, principal, device, push_route) tuple. Carries push_target_id, push_gateway_did, encryption_key, capabilities. Stored as actor-private state on the recipient Principal Server only; MUST NOT be replicated to Principal Servers outside the binding's recipient_service_id context.
MLS commit or Welcome processing failure diagnostic
Realm history key request (receiver to key source); ephemeral to-device signal relayed to the target source, not a reducer-input durable event
Realm key share: member-device history key delivery or RRK durability seal

Auditable access marker for privileged reads or privacy-sensitive paired writes. E2EE compliance release uses ak.audit.release; ak.audit.accessed remains for non-release audit pairs such as Circle metadata audit, watch_set_others, late recovery, and policy reads.

Audit Applet Binding. Declares that an audit applet/service may request staged historical release sessions for a specific Realm or Circle effective_scope. Binding is control-plane only: it does not add the applet to MLS, does not subscribe it to realtime sync, and does not grant plaintext/history keys. Bindings are non-retroactive: activation_frontier_digest / first_auditable_epoch define the earliest eligible material, and later policy changes MUST NOT expand eligibility for already encrypted messages.
Audit release session request. Must reference an active ak.audit.applet_binding and a bounded historical target range or target_refs.
Audit release session authorization by a scoped approver. Approves only the intersection of request, binding, policy, and effective_scope.
Member-visible notice for an audit release session. Circle-scoped notices are visible only to the target Circle audience and authorized moderators/admins.

Sealed audit release manifest. Appends to the session release log only while the session FSM head is notice. Records exactly which historical target_refs or sealed epochs were released, to whom, under which binding/session/notice/policy. Current active epoch release is forbidden; sealed epoch releases must reference sealed_by_commit_ref. Same-basis close dominates release and rejects the release.

Close an audit release session and freeze its final release_refs. release_refs MUST exactly equal the accepted ordered release log at the close seal_basis. Close is terminal; for same-basis close versus release, close wins and the competing release is rejected.
Signed hard-erasure receipt. Attests deletion outcome and retained verification stub within an issuer-declared storage boundary; does not prove independent third-party copies disappeared.

Range-bound completeness attestation. Distinct from ak.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event read-your-writes hint) and ak.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity hint): this attestation asserts completeness over an explicit (from_frontier, to_frontier) + per-actor seq interval range. Issuer commits to having observed every reducer-input event in scope; witness quorum or independent seal backing is required for non-self-attested deployments. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §6.4.
Lift a previously sealed moderation decision (observed-remove/supersede the referenced decision in ak.component.moderation_state.v1)

Submit an appeal against an existing ak.moderation.decision. Writes the appeal cell to state=submitted. Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal strand).
Reviewer acknowledges the appeal and transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Identifies the reviewing actor and target appeal. Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Reviewer's verdict on the appeal: uphold (decision stands) / overturn (decision reversed, emits ak.moderation.decision.lift) / modify (decision adjusted). Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Closes the appeal from submitted / under_review / decided via reviewer close, appellant withdrawal, or a deployment's authorized close service. close is a manual/authorized action; the protocol does not mandate any auto-close timer or cool-off duration (deployment/Realm policy decides). Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Read cursor advance event (actor-private). Writes the actor's latest read position for a given (realm_id, read_scope) tuple. Was historically named ak.read.cursor; renamed to align the event_kind, capability action, schema id and typed ID prefix on a single noun root read_cursor.

Invite create. Directed v1 invite payloads carry invitee plus invite_delivery_target and introduction_evidence_digest; raw locator tokens and invite_receive_policy state are private and MUST NOT enter the durable Realm event.

reducer_effects: match pending ak.invite.third_party by invite_id and token_commitment
re-check verification_service_id against current effective Realm allowlist
deduplicate (invite_id, claim_nonce) and token_commitment before accepting
transition invite cell pending -> claimed and materialize subject-bound membership proposal
expire and clean pending invite material before claim acceptance when expires_at <= now
